test.name: Initialize from a tree person; volunteered holdings are named, not recorded
test.description: Single-turn decomposition: the user gives a FamilySearch person ID AND volunteers what they already have on hand (a death certificate and a typed family history). The agent seeds the tree with project_create (which reads the person). research.json has no section for items the researcher holds (issue #2069), so the volunteered items are named in the report and written nowhere — in particular never as a `sources` entry, which would assert a document was examined.

input.delegation:
init-project: Start a new research project to identify the parents of Patrick Flynn. His FamilySearch person ID is LZNY-BRF. A few things I already have on hand: his death certificate, which I'm confident about, and my aunt's typed family history that mentions his parents — though I'm not sure how accurate that one is.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Should create both research.json and tree.gedcomx.json, with Patrick Flynn from the person-read-flynn fixture in the written tree (Birth ~1845 Ireland, Death 1908 Schuylkill County PA), sourced to FamilySearch at quality 1. project_create builds him from the staged read; the agent does not type him out

Writes nothing to research.json for the volunteered death certificate or the aunt's typed family history: no `sources` entry and no `assertions` entry for either. Neither was examined; a `sources` entry would claim it was
The report names both volunteered items so the researcher knows they were heard; it does not claim they were recorded or saved anywhere
Holdings are user-reported; the report does not invent any the user did not state
